title: A Lantern for the Bridge
premise: In the river city of Vellamark, 1899, Hazel Vane works her father's type foundry while the government's new census quietly sorts citizens into those who may stay and those who must go. When a census taker discovers her family's falsified papers, Hazel bargains with an ambitious official to secure one berth on the last evacuation barge of the century—knowing it can hold only one of them. She ultimately forges a document in her own hand that names her mother, sends her parents across together under one identity, and stays behind to keep the lantern lit over the bridge, becoming the anonymous printer whose underground broadsheets help spark the revolution she once feared.
about_author: Petra Oyelaran is a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century print shops across coastal Europe before turning to fiction. Her novels examine how ordinary hands—ink-stained, tired, precise—shape the documents that decide who belongs.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sorts
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In the Vane foundry, Hazel cuts type by lamplight while her father drills her on which possessions fit in one case. The census notices posted on the bridge introduce quiet dread. Emotional beat: the comfort of craft shadowed by the first tremor of displacement.

chapters.title: Questions in a Ledger
chapters.summary: Census taker Ambrose Kettle's POV. Kettle arrives to count the Vane household and notices the mother's name appears in no parish record. He records the discrepancy but hesitates to report it. Emotional beat: a bureaucrat's conscience flickering against ambition.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel alters a printed census form at night, practicing her father's hand. Her younger brother Tam catches her and swears silence. Emotional beat: guilty exhilaration—the first forgery, the first complicity.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Dusk
chapters.summary: Mother Ilse's POV. Ilse walks the bridge where refugees queue for registration stamps, recognizing neighbors who no longer meet her eye. She confesses nothing to Hazel but burns her old letters. Emotional beat: maternal sacrifice rehearsed in secret.

chapters.title: A Berth Is Promised
chapters.summary: Kettle's POV. Kettle's superior rewards his thoroughness; he is offered promotion if he delivers the Vane case as an example. He visits Hazel privately, offering to lose one page—for a price. Emotional beat: corruption dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The family inventories their lives into three cases. Father Aldous insists the type itself must travel; Hazel argues people matter more than lead. Their first real quarrel. Emotional beat: love expressed as argument over what defines them.

chapters.title: The Price of One Page
chapters.summary: Kettle's POV. Kettle names his price: the foundry's client ledger, implicating a magistrate. Hazel realizes he is building his own ladder from her family's bones. Emotional beat: revulsion braided with calculation.

chapters.title: Tam's Map
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Twelve-year-old Tam maps the sewers and coal chutes of Vellamark, convinced the family can hide instead of flee. His optimism cracks when he sees soldiers marking doors. Emotional beat: childhood ending early.

chapters.title: The Last Barge Announced
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Proclamation: one final barge before the century turns, berths assigned by lottery and favor. The city splits into those who wait and those who scheme. Emotional beat: collective panic, private resolve.

chapters.title: A Hand That Lies Well
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel perfects forged transit papers using her father's finest type. Aldous discovers her work—and instead of anger, teaches her the kerning tricks that make forgery undetectable. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as complicity.

chapters.title: Kettle Ascending
chapters.summary: Kettle's POV. Kettle delivers half the Vane file and is promoted to berth assignment. Power tastes better than he imagined; he begins erasing inconvenient pages for others too, for larger prices. Emotional beat: corruption completing its arc.

chapters.title: Three Names, One Berth
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse learns the truth of the bargain and secretly petitions Kettle to take only herself, leaving the children. He refuses—unless she brings him something worse than a ledger. Emotional beat: a mother bargaining with her own erasure.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Secret
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. To satisfy Kettle, Hazel prints a false confession bearing the magistrate's seal. Holding the finished page, she understands she has crossed from survivor into maker of fates. Emotional beat: cold clarity, grief for her former self.

chapters.title: Doors Marked in Chalk
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Soldiers chalk the foundry door for seizure. Tam scrubs it off and is nearly caught; a stranger in a printer's apron shields him—an underground network watching the Vanes. Emotional beat: fear met by unexpected solidarity.

chapters.title: The Night of the Lottery
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Public berth lottery descends into riot on the bridge. Hazel watches neighbors trample each other for paper slips and realizes the system was designed to make the desperate destroy themselves. Emotional beat: horror crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: What Kettle Wants
chapters.summary: Kettle's POV. Kettle demands the foundry itself in exchange for two berths, not one. Hazel counters: one berth, her silence about his erased pages, and the magistrate's confession held as insurance. Emotional beat: two schemers recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The family votes—or tries to. Aldous refuses to leave his type; Ilse refuses to leave Aldous; Tam volunteers to stay with Hazel. Hazel ends the deadlock alone: she will forge papers naming both parents under one identity. Emotional beat: terrible clarity of love as triage.

chapters.title: Last Type Standing
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. On the quay, Aldous abandons his life's type cases to board with Ilse, weeping as the barge takes them downriver. He presses his graver into Hazel's hands through the rail. Emotional beat: surrender as the deepest gift.

chapters.title: The Lantern Lit
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel and Tam return to the empty foundry. She hangs the bridge lantern, sets type for her first underground broadsheet, and signs it with no name at all. Emotional beat: loss transmuted into vocation.

chapters.title: Broadside Winter
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Through winter, brother and sister print and scatter truth sheets; the city begins repeating their words aloud. Kettle hunts the anonymous printer without knowing she lives above the old press. Emotional beat: dangerous hope taking root.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. New Year's Eve: crowds fill the bridge, and Kettle, exposed by his own erased pages surfacing in Hazel's broadsheets, falls from favor as the uprising ignites. Hazel watches from the lantern tower, unseen. Emotional beat: vindication without triumph.

chapters.title: A Letter Downriver
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Spring: a letter arrives from her parents, alive and settled. Hazel reads it by the lantern, then sets type for the next broadsheet. The bridge stands; so does she. Emotional beat: belonging redefined—not a place granted, but a light kept.
